scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS asked for an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-06).
Majority of disputed bills carry ACTUAL (correctly recorded) read type rather than ESTIMATED (E-01).
Manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target, affecting 9200 accounts, Aug-Sep 2026 (E-02).
Ticket response times remain within SLA, so handling speed is not lagging (E-05).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1200-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-06), driven primarily by a defect in the billing calculation/import-validation step that produces incorrect bills even when the underlying meter read was correctly recorded as ACTUAL: disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL (1785) over ESTIMATED (1240) reads (E-01), ruling out estimate-substitution (AMI or field read gaps) as the primary driver. No tariff change occurred this year (E-03, E-04) and ticket response times remain within SLA (E-05), so neither tariff shifts nor slow handling explain the surge; degraded manual-read route completion (0.88 vs 0.95 target, 9200 accounts, E-02) is at most a secondary contributor.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-12: re-read under E-12 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-12 strengthens the primary import-validation-defect driver but shows the 'secondary' estimated-bill stream it attributes to route completion is actually explained by the same AMI import-rejection mechanism, so the two-cause framing in the root statement needs narrowing/revision.; PR-CHAIN-5: All 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills trace to AMI-channel read events (1184 rejected at import, 56 no-read), not to manual-read route lateness, so route-completion is not the mechanism producing this estimated-bill stream as claimed.

This indicates nearly all ESTIMATED-read disputes stem from a billing-import validation rule rejecting legitimate high-consumption AMI reads rather than from missing reads or manual field-read delivery failures.

U-RULES-CHANGE-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Did a change to billing import validation rules (e.g., estimate-substitution logic or read-acceptance thresholds) around August 2026 cause the calculation defect behind most disputed ACTUAL-read bills?

U-TICKET-MEASUREMENT-ARTIFACT.safe_placeholder: Continue monitoring raw dispute_volume_trend while flagging the possible measurement-artifact caveat.

U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: AMI-event verification deferred; current scope relies on billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type (E-01), which already weighs against AMI as the primary driver.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VERIFIC.decision_impact: Determines whether staffing specifically, versus other causes, explains the route-completion shortfall, affecting secondary-remediation design.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CLAIM-VERIFIC.safe_placeholder: Treat the route-completion shortfall as a secondary contributor without attributing root cause to staffing specifically.
